what: Several background-colored vertical bars covering the hero start in random order (all within .5s) and lift up 98% over 2s expo.inOut, so the screen below is revealed unevenly. Once all are lifted, the curtain is hidden and fx:done fires

options.amount: Total time over which bar starts are spread (sec), default .5
options.step: Stretch bar i’s height to screen + i×step (css length) — even when they lift by the same length, the bottom edge rises stepwise one after another in a staircase shape (original 5.787vw). Bars stick to the top
options.lift: Share revealed (%), default 98 — 100 means all the way
options.--fx-fill: Bar color (via style), default var(--kf-bg) — for the ink-dark curtain use var(--kf-contrast-bg)

note: A part that makes people wait — on frequently flipped screens, use a shorter dur. The source site only defines this cover and never uses it

from.where: Original common.js Overlay.showLoad(.overlay__mask .bar → yPercent -98, 2s expo.inOut, stagger amount .5 from random) — it exists only in the bundle, and the recorded page HTML has no bars, so it doesn’t run on the actual screen. A part whose numbers were only read from the original code

index.html .mk-splash (first page, once per session) — original splash-screen: four ink-black plates (height 100%+0·5.787·11.574·17.361vw) scale on Y from 1→0 with the top as the axis, 2.56s keyframes: hold at 0~25%, then 25~66.4% cubic-bezier(.44,.52,.14,1) (that is, hold .64s after .3s, then 1.06s), and fade out in .3s at 2.86s. Blocking wheel and touch in the meantime is up to the site.
